features.name: Landing_Page
features.purpose: Introduces BWS4 to visitors, explains that the platform and all its example apps were built using Spec4, and provides a navigable list of the available example apps.

invocation.trigger: A user navigates to the application's entry point.

inputs.name: example_app_listing
inputs.description: Name, short description, and entry point for each available example app.

outputs.primary: An introductory explanation of BWS4 and a browsable list of example apps
outputs.format: Structured page with text and navigable entries
outputs.schema_notes: Each list entry includes a name, short description, and a way to open that example app.

success_criteria: Every currently available example app appears in the list
Selecting an entry opens the corresponding example app
The explanation clearly states BWS4 and its apps were built with Spec4

failure_modes.mode: A newly added example app does not appear in the list
failure_modes.mitigation: Maintain a single authoritative source describing all available example apps that this page always reads from

failure_modes.mode: An entry links to an app that fails to open
failure_modes.mitigation: Verify each listed entry resolves to a working example app before it is shown

features.name: RAG_Example_App
features.purpose: Demonstrates the retrieval-augmented generation pattern by answering user questions using a small public dataset, showing how retrieved information grounds a generated answer.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the RAG example app and submits a question.

inputs.name: reference_dataset
inputs.description: A small, publicly available set of documents the app can search over.

inputs.name: user_question
inputs.description: The question the user wants answered.

outputs.primary: A generated answer grounded in retrieved passages
outputs.format: Text answer accompanied by the source passages used
outputs.schema_notes: Includes the answer text plus a list of the specific passages that informed it.

success_criteria: Retrieved passages are topically relevant to the question
The generated answer reflects content actually present in the retrieved passages
Sources used are visibly shown alongside the answer

failure_modes.mode: Retrieval returns passages unrelated to the question
failure_modes.mitigation: Use a curated, well-scoped dataset and verify retrieval quality against sample questions
Fall back to an alternate available language provider
Reject empty input before attempting retrieval

features.name: Shared_Framework_Services
features.purpose: Provides the common capabilities every example app relies on: generating language responses across multiple providers (including free-tier options), producing text embeddings with a single shared embedding model, and storing and retrieving small amounts of app data.

invocation.trigger: An example app requests language generation, a text embedding, or a data read/write operation.

inputs.name: generation_request
inputs.description: Text an example app wants a language response for.

inputs.name: embedding_request
inputs.description: Text an example app wants converted into a numeric semantic representation.

inputs.name: data_operation
inputs.description: A request to save or fetch small pieces of app data.

outputs.primary: Language responses, embedding vectors, and stored/retrieved data made available to requesting example apps
outputs.format: Text responses, numeric vectors, and structured records
outputs.schema_notes: The same embedding representation and storage behavior is used consistently across all example apps.

success_criteria: Any example app can obtain a language response without separately configuring its own provider
Any example app can obtain an embedding vector using the one shared embedding model
Data saved by an app can later be retrieved correctly
Behavior is consistent no matter which example app is calling

failure_modes.mode: A given language provider is temporarily unavailable or rate-limited
failure_modes.mitigation: Automatically try an alternate available free-tier provider

failure_modes.mode: Different apps end up using inconsistent embedding representations
failure_modes.mitigation: Enforce a single shared embedding model used by all apps

failure_modes.mode: Stored data becomes unavailable or unreadable
failure_modes.mitigation: Detect and clearly report data access issues rather than failing silently

features.name: Tool_Use_Integration
features.purpose: Lets example apps that need real-world, up-to-date information issue external search lookups, illustrating the tool-use agentic pattern.

invocation.trigger: An example app's logic determines it needs external information and issues a search request.

inputs.name: search_query
inputs.description: The query text to search for.

inputs.name: result_limit
inputs.description: Optional cap on how many results to return.

outputs.primary: A list of relevant external search results
outputs.format: List of items, each with a title, short snippet, and reference link
outputs.schema_notes: Results are ordered by relevance to the query.

success_criteria: Returned results are topically relevant to the search query
Requesting example app can incorporate results into its own response
No results is communicated clearly rather than treated as an error

failure_modes.mode: Free usage allowance for search is exhausted
failure_modes.mitigation: Detect the limit and inform the requesting app so it can degrade gracefully
Report the empty outcome explicitly to the requesting app
Validate the query before issuing the search

features.name: Embeddings_Example_App
features.purpose: Visually demonstrates the embedding pattern by plotting a curated set of texts in a 2D space based on semantic similarity, letting users add their own text and see it placed among the rest, alongside a short explanation of what embeddings are.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the embeddings example app, or submits custom text within it.

inputs.name: preconfigured_examples
inputs.description: A built-in curated set of words, short phrases, and sentences spanning multiple categories.

inputs.name: custom_text
inputs.description: Text entered by the user to be embedded and placed among the existing examples.

outputs.primary: A 2D visual plot of all texts positioned by semantic similarity, plus an educational explanation of the embedding pattern
outputs.format: Interactive visual plot with distinctly marked custom entries, accompanied by explanatory text
outputs.schema_notes: Each plotted point is labeled with its source text; custom-entered points are visually distinguishable from the preconfigured ones.

success_criteria: Preconfigured examples visibly cluster by semantic category (e.g. animals near animals, emotions near emotions)
Submitting custom text adds it to the same plot, recalculated to include it
Custom text points are clearly visually distinct from preconfigured points
The explanation of the embedding pattern is present and understandable
The app follows the same layout as other example apps and is reachable from the landing page and navigation menu

failure_modes.mode: The plot layout shifts drastically each time custom text is added, making comparison hard
failure_modes.mitigation: Apply the same projection approach consistently across recalculations

failure_modes.mode: Custom text points are not visually distinguishable from preconfigured points
failure_modes.mitigation: Enforce a distinct visual treatment for user-submitted points

failure_modes.mode: This app ends up using a different embedding representation than other apps
failure_modes.mitigation: Require use of the one shared embedding model rather than a separate one
Validate input before attempting to embed and plot it

nfr_goals: All example apps present a consistent, unified look and navigation experience
The platform operates using only free-tier language, embedding, and search resources
New example apps can be added without disrupting existing ones
Interactions within example apps feel responsive enough for live demonstration
The system degrades gracefully and communicates clearly when a free-tier usage limit is reached
